summary: Equity medians (geometric, nominal USD) put US large cap lowest at 6.0% (n=8), below Japan 6.4% (n=4), US small cap 6.5% (n=6), global 6.8% (n=6), EM 8.0% (n=7) and Europe 8.1% (n=4).
Among n≥4 rows, IQRs are tightest in bonds: EM local debt 5.3% (IQR 20bp, n=5), US IG 5.4% (23bp, n=6), intermediate Treasuries 4.9% (24bp, n=8), high yield 5.9% (27bp, n=8); cash 3.7% (n=6).
Private equity has the highest median of any row, 9.7% (n=5); private credit is 7.0% (n=4), commodities 5.7% (n=7), hedge funds 5.5% (n=4).
Ranked by IQR among n≥4 rows, the widest disagreements are EM equity (250bp), commodities (171bp), US small cap (165bp) and private equity (155bp); UK equity's 270bp rests on three publishers.
This site's LTCMA sits furthest below the public median on commodities (3.5% vs 5.7%, n=7), UK equity (7.0% vs 8.9%, n=3), China equity (7.4% vs 8.5%, n=3) and high yield (5.0% vs 5.9%, n=8).
This site's LTCMA is also 40bp below the median on cash, intermediate Treasuries and US IG (n=6-8), and above on developed ex-US equity (7.7% vs 7.1%, n=3); gold: 3.3% vs one publisher's 1.6%.
Markets price a 25bp hike at the next FOMC at 88.5% on both venues (hold 2.4-3.5%) and no cuts in 2026 at 98.0-98.2%, consistent with Invesco's expected hikes, not Goldman Sachs AM's easing path.

A US recession starting in 2026 is priced at 2.0-2.3%, consistent with expansion base cases (Robeco, Mercer, Goldman Sachs AM) and with PIMCO, whose credit-loss call sits on a resilient-growth baseline.

divergence_rule: public IQR >= 150bp with n >= 4, or >= 1 overweight and >= 1 underweight stance

divergences.label: US large cap
divergences.headline: US large cap (median 6.0%, n=8): AI-led earnings growth versus valuation drag; Ninety One the low outlier at 1.7%.

bull.argument: AQR, T. Rowe Price, Fidelity International and BNY Investments sit at 6.3-7.6%. BNY Investments assumes AI-lifted earnings with multiples held flat; Fidelity International adds AI-driven revenue growth, dividends and buybacks; AQR and T. Rowe Price land here despite noting rich valuations. Goldman Sachs AM is overweight on the earnings strength of mega-caps and sustained AI spending.
bull.data_used: Earnings-growth building blocks (real GDP, AI-boosted revenue and EPS), income, buybacks and inflation; constant valuation multiples (BNY Investments).

bear.argument: Ninety One, State Street, Invesco and Vanguard sit at 1.7-5.7%. Ninety One's record-low figure reflects one of the largest revaluation hits; Invesco and Vanguard see high valuations offsetting stronger earnings. PIMCO, Lazard and Amundi are underweight: PIMCO puts the equity risk premium near zero versus bonds, Lazard doubts US resilience and expects allocators to rotate away.
bear.data_used: Starting valuations and multiple-change building blocks, revaluation impact (Ninety One), and a near-zero equity risk premium versus bonds (PIMCO).

divergences.what_to_watch: Whether AI-driven EPS growth persists at current multiples (high side) or multiples de-rate and margins mean-revert (low side), and the equity risk premium versus Treasury yields.

divergences.label: US small cap
divergences.headline: US small cap (IQR 165bp, n=6): valuation and rate-cut optimism versus weaker long-run earnings growth.

bull.argument: BNY Investments, AQR and Vanguard sit at 6.6-7.5%. Vanguard ranks small caps above large caps after recent weakness; AQR uses local real return plus inflation; BNY Investments assumes a weak size premium, leaving small caps just below its broad US figure. Goldman Sachs AM is overweight on attractive valuations, anticipated Fed cuts, faster earnings growth and reviving M&A.
bull.data_used: Valuations after recent underperformance, factor and real-return models, and an expected Fed easing path (Goldman Sachs AM).

bear.argument: State Street, Invesco and T. Rowe Price sit at 5.0-6.3%. Invesco's figure rose as valuation drag shrank, yet weaker long-run earnings growth leaves small caps trailing mid caps; State Street's dividend, earnings-growth and multiple-change blocks put it lowest; T. Rowe Price's valuation-anchored figure was selectively upgraded but stays below the median.
bear.data_used: Long-run earnings-growth assumptions, dividend yield and valuation-change building blocks, and valuation-anchored forecasting.

divergences.what_to_watch: Small-cap earnings growth relative to large caps, and the Fed path: markets price a 25bp hike at the next FOMC at 88.5% on both venues, undercutting the rate-cut argument.

divergences.label: EM equity
divergences.headline: EM equity, widest IQR among rows with n≥4 (250bp): earnings and weaker-dollar optimism versus valuation-anchored low estimates.

bull.argument: Robeco, T. Rowe Price and BNY Investments (8.1-8.8%) cite earnings momentum, GDP-driven earnings, currency gains and rising middle powers. Overweights: BlackRock Investment Institute (high conviction) on robust earnings and lower valuations; Goldman Sachs AM on a weaker dollar, cheaper oil and Fed easing; Amundi and CIBC Asset Management. Fidelity International sits exactly at the 8.0% median.
bull.data_used: Five-year horizons (Robeco, T. Rowe Price); forward-earnings rebound; real GDP growth into earnings; P/E discount to the US; dollar and Fed path.

bear.argument: Ninety One, Vanguard and Invesco sit at 3.7-7.1%. Ninety One's currency-hedged figure is in the bottom quartile of its history after negative revaluation; Vanguard raised its view on easing valuations yet stays far below the median, flagging the highest volatility among equity classes; Invesco, unchanged, relies on currency and dividends, contingent on earnings delivery.
bear.data_used: Starting valuations and revaluation effects, a currency-hedged basis (Ninety One) that strips out currency gains, dividends and earnings-delivery risk.

divergences.what_to_watch: EM forward earnings revisions, the P/E discount to the US and the dollar trend; a next-FOMC 25bp hike priced at 88.5% on both venues challenges the Fed-cut leg.

divergences.label: US high yield
divergences.headline: US high yield: tight numbers (IQR 27bp, n=8; three at the median) but stances split over a default cycle.

bull.argument: Ninety One and BNY Investments sit above the 5.9% median, up to 6.3%. Ninety One credits higher Treasury yields despite tight spreads; BNY Investments stays above the median even after assuming spreads widen toward their long-run median. Goldman Sachs AM is overweight for income, citing healthy interest coverage, limited defaults, an upgraded ratings mix and M&A-driven demand.
bull.data_used: Higher Treasury yields, default losses set as a share of projected spread (BNY Investments), interest coverage, ratings mix and M&A-driven demand.

bear.argument: AQR, T. Rowe Price and State Street sit at 5.0-5.7%; the latter two net spread widening or default risk against carry. PIMCO's underweight targets lower-quality cyclical issuers, treating tight spreads as mispriced risk while defaults start to climb; Amundi is also underweight. Vanguard, Invesco and Fidelity International, at the median, are on neither side.
bear.data_used: Default-probability adjustments to yield, carry versus spread widening, real return plus inflation (AQR), and rising lower-quality credit stress (PIMCO).

divergences.what_to_watch: Default and recovery rates among lower-quality issuers, and whether spreads widen from near historic tights toward their long-run median.

divergences.label: Commodities
divergences.headline: Commodities (IQR 171bp, n=7): futures risk-premium and inflation-hedge cases versus low roll-return and dollar-based estimates.

bull.argument: AQR, Invesco and Robeco sit at 5.8-6.7%. AQR adds a long-run futures premium over cash to the expected real cash return; Invesco stresses direct exposure to inflation and supply shocks; Robeco ties outcomes to conflicts and the dollar. Vanguard, at the 5.7% median, and neutral Mercer are on neither side.
bull.data_used: Long-run futures excess return over cash plus real cash rates (AQR); inflation and supply-shock sensitivity; geopolitical and dollar scenarios.

bear.argument: BNY Investments, State Street and T. Rowe Price sit at 2.3-5.2%. State Street combines US inflation and dollar forecasts with roll yield, positioning and collateral income; BNY Investments projects weak returns with high volatility and gives no drivers; T. Rowe Price offers no asset-specific rationale.
bear.data_used: US inflation and dollar index forecasts, futures roll return, positioning and collateral return (State Street); BNY Investments and T. Rowe Price disclose no drivers.

divergences.what_to_watch: Futures roll yield (backwardation versus contango) and collateral returns, plus inflation surprises and the dollar's direction.

divergences.label: Global equity (ACWI)
divergences.headline: Global equity (IQR 100bp, n=6): earnings-led estimates versus valuation-anchored ones, with Ninety One the outlier at 2.8%.

bull.argument: Robeco and BNY Investments hold the two highest estimates, up to 7.8%. Robeco, proxying with developed equities, sees earnings growth outrunning an expected de-rating; BNY Investments aggregates cap-weighted regional income, earnings and currency estimates, consistent with the central path of its Monte Carlo simulation. T. Rowe Price, at the 6.8% median, is on neither side.
bull.data_used: Cap-weighted regional income, earnings-growth and currency estimates in a Monte Carlo framework (BNY Investments); earnings growth net of multiple compression (Robeco).

bear.argument: Ninety One, Invesco and Fidelity International sit at 2.8-6.7%. Ninety One sees rich valuations, above all in the US, pinning returns close to historical lows; Invesco notes weaker earnings growth and reduced buybacks; Fidelity International is overweight yet just below the median, with above-equilibrium margins offsetting AI-driven growth. PIMCO is underweight on bonds' better prospective Sharpe ratio.
bear.data_used: Starting valuations, notably US; margins versus equilibrium; buybacks and earnings growth; prospective bond-versus-equity Sharpe ratios (PIMCO).

divergences.what_to_watch: US valuation multiples and global earnings growth versus multiple compression, and how high-quality bond yields move relative to equity earnings yields.

divergences.label: Global govt bonds
divergences.headline: Global government bonds: tight numbers (IQR 39bp, n=4); PIMCO's highest-conviction overweight versus BNY Investments' fiscal-strain underweight.

bull.argument: Robeco and Ninety One sit at 5.3%, both on USD-hedged sovereign composites, crediting higher starting yields. PIMCO, without a number, rates global government bonds its highest-conviction overweight: out-of-sync cycles and divergent policy paths supply income, diversification and active country and curve opportunities.
bull.data_used: Starting yields on USD-hedged sovereign composites, and cross-country divergence in growth and policy paths (PIMCO).

bear.argument: Invesco and Fidelity International sit at 4.8-4.9%, both income-driven estimates anchored on starting yields; Fidelity International is nonetheless overweight, expecting sovereigns to hedge recessions. BNY Investments, without a number, is underweight, arguing fiscal pressure erodes sovereigns' risk-adjusted appeal and looking to real assets and private markets to diversify. Neutral Mercer is on neither side.
bear.data_used: Starting yields as the income driver (Invesco, Fidelity International); fiscal strain and steeper curves weighing on sovereign duration (BNY Investments).

divergences.what_to_watch: Term premia and curve steepness under fiscal strain, and whether sovereigns rally in equity drawdowns, i.e. the stock-bond correlation.

divergences.label: Private equity
divergences.headline: Private equity (IQR 155bp, n=5): whether an illiquidity premium survives fees; Fidelity International sits at the 9.7% median.

bull.argument: BNY Investments and T. Rowe Price sit above the median, up to 10.5%, both citing an illiquidity premium; BNY Investments layers it on public-equity factor exposure as private capital funds AI and infrastructure, T. Rowe Price adds active management. BlackRock Investment Institute flags venture capital as a high-conviction alpha source; CIBC Asset Management is also overweight.
bull.data_used: Public-equity factor exposure plus an illiquidity premium (BNY Investments); Cambridge Associates global PE benchmark and active management (T. Rowe Price).

bear.argument: AQR and State Street sit below the median, with AQR at the 6.6% low end. AQR uses a levered DDM for US buyouts after fees; cheaper debt and multiple expansion raised its figure, yet it sees private-asset risk premia compressed against positive real cash. State Street extrapolates past fund returns, comparable to levered listed equity after fees.
bear.data_used: Levered DDM for US buyouts net of fees (AQR); historical fund performance versus leverage-adjusted listed equity (State Street).

divergences.what_to_watch: Net-of-fee buyout returns versus leverage-adjusted listed equity, deal financing costs, and whether elevated dry powder pushes up entry multiples.

divergences.label: Private credit
divergences.headline: Private credit (IQR 127bp, n=4): overweights dominate, but PIMCO's high-conviction underweight cites rising stress and higher losses.

bull.argument: T. Rowe Price and State Street sit at 7.2-9.2%, T. Rowe Price citing an illiquidity premium and structural demand for private lending. Goldman Sachs AM is overweight on a yield pickup over public credit and lower historical defaults than syndicated loans; BlackRock Investment Institute backs only selected strategies. Amundi and CIBC Asset Management are also overweight.
bull.data_used: Direct-lending benchmark history (Cliffwater), senior private debt benchmark (State Street), illiquidity premium, yield pickup and relative default history.

bear.argument: AQR and Fidelity International sit at 5.0-6.9%. AQR models private credit as modestly levered floating-rate high yield whose fees absorb any illiquidity premium; Fidelity International is overweight yet just below the median, seeing no immediate stress. PIMCO's high-conviction underweight cites rising PIK use, maturity extensions and markedly higher expected losses in middle-market direct lending, excluding asset-based finance.
bear.data_used: Floating-rate high-yield model with leverage and fees (AQR); PIK usage, maturity extensions and stress indicators in direct lending (PIMCO).

divergences.what_to_watch: Non-accruals, PIK share and maturity extensions in middle-market direct lending, and realized losses versus syndicated loans.
